raw_record.question_text: In the diagram, one should go from A to B along the arrows. Along the way, calculate the sum of the numbers that are stepped on. How many different results can be obtained?

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a 3-by-3 directed grid of numbered circles between A and B. From the image, the bottom row is 1,2,1; the middle row is 2,3,2; the top row is 1,2,1. All arrows go only right or upward, so every route from A to B corresponds to choosing an order of two right moves and two up moves after entering the bottom-left 1. Enumerate the six possible move orders: RRUU, RURU, RUUR, URRU, URUR, UURR. For each path, add the numbers of the five circles stepped on. The two outer-edge paths give 7, while the four paths through the center 3 give 9. Therefore the set of possible sums has size 2.
